inputsRead.coverage: all 14 shot frames and all 59 dense frames at 1.5-second cadence were visually reviewed; the 28 cue-frame mappings/timestamps were reviewed from the evidence index, and key dense frames were enlarged in-memory for legibility

mediaFacts.subtitleCaveat: Provided subtitles contain obvious ASR/character errors. Claim wording was cross-checked against burned-in captions and visible frames where possible.

verdict.summary: The video is a promotional Qwen2 overview, not a controlled Qwen2-versus-GPT-4 test. It shows Qwen2 pages, model-card tables, social posts and demo screenshots, but no GPT-4 run, no shared prompt, no timing/cost protocol and no blind grading. Its own benchmark tables include Qwen2 losses to Llama 3, so '全面碾压' is not supported as a comprehensive claim. A visible license paragraph distinguishes Qwen2-72B from Apache-2.0 models, but the narration collapses access, open source and free use into one unqualified recommendation.

headline.visibleText: 国产AI碾压GPT4? 学霸级模型免费用!
headline.assessment: The question-mark headline suggests a GPT-4 comparison, but the body never performs or displays one.

modelVersions.qwen2: Family and several sizes are shown; the narration emphasizes Qwen2-72B and 128K context.
modelVersions.gpt4: Only the generic label GPT-4 is spoken/shown; no dated snapshot or product/API variant is identified.

qwen2VersusGpt4.groundTruth: The creator says she previously recommended GPT-4 but now recommends free domestic open models. That is a personal recommendation and cost/open-access argument, not evidence that Qwen2 beats GPT-4 on any specific task.

qwen2Family.caveat: The spoken 'from 0.5B to 72B' range is directionally visible, but it is not a claim that every intermediate size exists. The video alternates between a five-size family listing and a four-column specification table.

benchmarkLimits: No GPT-4 column appears in the visible benchmark tables.
The video does not state evaluation-harness versions, prompts/templates, decoding settings, checkpoints, quantization, hardware, sample counts, confidence intervals or test dates.
The tables are displayed as screenshots/model-card material; the creator does not reproduce the runs.
The narration groups multimodal processing, multilingual understanding, reasoning and code generation together, but the displayed benchmark material does not establish a multimodal-input evaluation.

visibleTasksAndInterfaces.visibleContent: Qwen2 logo, documentation/model links, family sizes, language count and context-length table; a model listing also includes official and community/quantized variants.
visibleTasksAndInterfaces.whatItProves: The video contains Qwen2 documentation/listing material and identifies multiple family sizes.
visibleTasksAndInterfaces.whatItDoesNotProve: It does not prove model quality against GPT-4 or unrestricted/free deployment.

visibleTasksAndInterfaces.interface: Qwen2 model-card benchmark tables and charts
visibleTasksAndInterfaces.visibleContent: Base and instruction-tuned comparisons against named Llama 3, Mixtral, Qwen1.5 and GLM4 variants, plus code/math charts.
visibleTasksAndInterfaces.whatItProves: Specific benchmark numbers and named opponents are visually asserted by the source page.
visibleTasksAndInterfaces.whatItDoesNotProve: The creator did not independently run or validate them, and the tables do not support an exceptionless win over Llama 3.

visibleTasksAndInterfaces.visibleContent: Posts attributed on screen to Clement Delangue and Yuchen Jin praise Qwen2-72B and refer to the Hugging Face Open LLM Leaderboard and LiveBench.
visibleTasksAndInterfaces.whatItProves: At least two favorable posts are shown.
visibleTasksAndInterfaces.whatItDoesNotProve: The video does not authenticate the posts, explain the referenced leaderboards, or establish that all industry authorities agree.

visibleTasksAndInterfaces.visibleContent: A Qwen2 node appears to expand a cat-image prompt inside a workflow, with generated cat images displayed below.
visibleTasksAndInterfaces.whatItProves: A screenshot of one apparent Qwen2-assisted application workflow is shown.
visibleTasksAndInterfaces.whatItDoesNotProve: No live interaction, repository, model checkpoint, input/output trace or adoption count is shown; it also does not demonstrate that Qwen2 itself accepts multimodal input.

visibleTasks: Write python code for fib(n) to compute the nth Fibonacci number
visibleTasksAndInterfaces.visibleOutput: A tomato joke and a short recursive Fibonacci function are shown as already-present responses.
visibleTasksAndInterfaces.whatItProves: The video shows two simple Qwen demo outputs.
visibleTasksAndInterfaces.whatItDoesNotProve: The responses are not generated continuously on camera, the code is not executed or tested, and GPT-4 is not given either task.

visibleTasksAndInterfaces.visibleContent: Two answers about options trading are shown under selectors that appear to name Llama3-70B and Qwen2-72B variants.
visibleTasksAndInterfaces.whatItDoesNotProve: The full prompt, system prompts, settings, model endpoints, generation trace, latency and grading are absent. No winner is demonstrated, and GPT-4 is not present.

licenseAndCost.visibleLicenseStatement: The model-card frame says that models other than Qwen2-72B base/instruct are Apache 2.0, while Qwen2-72B still uses the original Qianwen License.
licenseAndCost.assessment: This is a material qualification to the narration's blanket 'open source' framing, especially because the 72B model is the video's featured version. The exact rights, restrictions and commercial-use conditions of the Qianwen License are not explained. Opponent licenses are not shown or discussed.
licenseAndCost.freeClaim: The video does not define free. It gives no API price, download charge, hosting cost, GPU requirement, electricity cost or total-cost comparison. A downloadable model can still incur deployment and inference costs.
unknowns: Whether the promoted packaged build is free of charge
Whether the package contains weights or only setup instructions
Whether the use case is permitted by the relevant model license
What compute is required for the 72B model
What GPT-4 price/product/date is being compared

claimAudit.claim: Qwen2 is currently the world's hottest open-source model.
claimAudit.reason: Model pages and favorable posts are visible, but no market-wide popularity measure, date-bounded ranking methodology or adoption data supports 'the world's hottest'.

claimAudit.claim: Qwen2 spans 0.5B to 72B, and the 72B version has 128K context.
claimAudit.reason: The size range and the 72B 128K value are visible on the Qwen2 page. The family listing also shows 57B-A14B, while the four-column specification table omits it.

claimAudit.claim: Qwen2 handles multimodality, multilingual understanding, reasoning and code generation.
claimAudit.reason: Language, reasoning and code benchmarks/demos are shown. The Stable Diffusion workflow shows Qwen2 producing a text prompt, not Qwen2 accepting or reasoning over multimodal input; no controlled task validates the bundled claim.

The displayed tables contain multiple Llama 3 wins: Llama3-70B-Instruct exceeds Qwen2-72B-Instruct on MBPP (82.3 vs 80.2) and GSM8K (93.0 vs 91.1); Llama3-8B-Instruct exceeds Qwen2-7B-Instruct on HumanEval (82.2 vs 79.9). Many other cells favor Qwen2, but that supports a selective/mixed benchmark conclusion, not an exceptionless comprehensive win.

claimAudit.claim: Top AI authorities are unanimously praising Qwen2.
claimAudit.reason: Two favorable social-post screenshots are shown. Two examples do not establish unanimity across top industry authorities, and their claims are not independently verified inside the video.

claimAudit.claim: Overseas developers are using Qwen2 to build AI applications.
claimAudit.reason: A workflow screenshot supplies one apparent example, but no developer identity, repository, usage trace or adoption count is given.
No OpenAI product page, price, license/availability comparison or dated product version is shown. 'Arrogant' is rhetoric rather than a testable performance claim.

claimAudit.claim: Users should stop paying for GPT-4 and directly use free domestic open models.
claimAudit.reason: There is no same-task GPT-4 comparison, no user/use-case segmentation and no total-cost analysis. The featured Qwen2-72B has a visible license exception, and self-hosting cost is not addressed.

claimAudit.claim: Jensen Huang strongly praised Meta's open-source model and said large AI models should be open source.
claimAudit.reason: The opening shows Jensen Huang and Mark Zuckerberg in an interview setting, but no source/date, audible quotation transcript or on-screen full quote is supplied. The footage alone cannot establish the exact paraphrase.

claimAudit.claim: The creator has packaged Qwen2 and can arrange it via comments.
claimAudit.reason: The spoken CTA is present, but the package, contents, installation method, safety and license compliance are not shown.

unknowns: Exact publication date and which Qwen2 checkpoint/revision was used in every screenshot
Which GPT-4 version, access tier and date the recommendation refers to
Whether any displayed response was generated by the creator rather than copied from a demo
The full prompt and settings behind the Qwen2/Llama side-by-side options-trading responses
Whether the benchmark tables were current at publication time and whether contamination controls were applied
Whether the social posts and leaderboard positions remained current outside the captured moment
The exact Qianwen License rights/restrictions and whether the promoted use falls within them
Real deployment cost and hardware requirements for Qwen2-72B
The contents and provenance of the promised packaged build
minimumSafeConclusion: The footage supports that Qwen2 was presented as a multi-size model family with a 72B/128K variant, favorable model-card benchmark results and some demo/application screenshots. It does not support the headline implication that Qwen2 was tested head-to-head against GPT-4, does not establish that Qwen2 is the right replacement for GPT-4 across uses, and does not support the absolute claim that it beats Llama 3 on every displayed benchmark.
